newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares turn higher after weak start.
newsitem.headline: French shares turn higher after weak start.

text.p: French shares bounced back on Tuesday morning after a sharp fall on Monday with investors awaiting President Jacques Chirac's television speech this evening.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 6.20 points or 0.23 percent at 2,660.94 after a 3.9 percent drop on Monday on the back of a stronger than expected showing of the left wing parties in the first round of parliamentary elections on Sunday.
Traders said the market was bouncing back in line with higher prices on other European stockmarkets. They said domestic investors were on the buying side again.
The market was mixed about Prime Minister Alain Juppe's decision to stand down after the runoff on June 1.
Investors are also waiting to see the far right National Front's instructions to its voters for the second round.
"Bonds have recovered, the franc seems to be holding up well, the dollar is climbing," said one share analyst.
